title: Mlai senior systemdesign retraining pipeline
question: How would you design an automated retraining pipeline for this, and what safeguards would you put in place before a new model goes live?
idealAnswer:
An automated pipeline should trigger retraining on a defined cadence and/or in response to detected drift or performance degradation, rather than a person remembering to do it manually

The pipeline needs to reliably pull fresh labeled data, accounting for label delay, e.g. waiting for confirmed fraud or chargeback outcomes, and apply the exact same feature engineering used in production, to avoid training and serving skew

Automated evaluation gates, the newly retrained model must be validated against held-out data and ideally recent production traffic, and should beat the current production model by some margin before being considered for promotion, not promoted automatically just because it finished training

A staged rollout for the new model, shadow mode or canary traffic, before full promotion, so a bad retrain is caught on a small slice of traffic rather than the full production audience

Versioning and rollback capability, every retrained model, its training data snapshot, and its evaluation results should be tracked so any live model can be reproduced or reverted quickly

A human-in-the-loop checkpoint for a sensitive model like fraud, e.g. requiring a person to review evaluation results before final promotion, rather than fully unattended automation for something this consequential
